questions.subject: Civil Engineering
questions.questionMarkup: Which of the following statement is correct for vane shear test?
questions.questionText: Which of the following statement is correct for vane shear test?

options.html: It is suitable for sands and dry soils.
options.text: It is suitable for sands and dry soils.

options.html: There is no mechanism to measure pore water pressure.
options.text: There is no mechanism to measure pore water pressure.

options.html: There is mechanism to measure pore water pressure.
options.text: There is mechanism to measure pore water pressure.

questions.explanationHtml:
(b)
Limitations of vane shear test:
• There is no mechanism to measure pore water pressure.
• It is not suitable for sand and dry soils.
• Drainage can’t be controlled.

questions.subject: Civil Engineering
questions.questionMarkup: Which of the following is not the assumption of Rankine’s earth pressure theory?
questions.questionText: Which of the following is not the assumption of Rankine’s earth pressure theory?

options.html: The soil mass is homogeneous and semi-infinite.
options.text: The soil mass is homogeneous and semi-infinite.

options.html: The ground surface is plane, which may be horizontal or inclined.
options.text: The ground surface is plane, which may be horizontal or inclined.

options.html: The back of the retaining wall is rough and vertical.
options.text: The back of the retaining wall is rough and vertical.

options.html: The soil element is in a state of plastic equilibrium.
options.text: The soil element is in a state of plastic equilibrium.

questions.explanationHtml:
(c)
Rankine (1857) considered the equilibrium of soil element within a soil mass bounded by a plane
surface.
The following assumptions are made in Rankine’s earth pressure theory:
• The soil mass is homogeneous and semi-infinite.
• The soil is dry and cohesionless.
• The ground surface is plane, which may be horizontal or inclined.
• The back of the retaining wall is smooth and vertical.
• The soil element is in a state of plastic equilibrium.
